root.label: optional, variant, any
root.note: Three vocabulary types for a value that may be absent, one of a closed set, or anything.

children.label: optional
children.note: A T or nothing, stored inline with no allocation.

children.label: Accessors
children.note: operator* on an empty optional is undefined behavior; value() throws bad_optional_access.

children.label: Assignment
children.note: Constructs, assigns or destroys depending on which side is engaged; emplace destroys then constructs.

children.label: optional<bool> trap
children.note: if (opt) tests engagement, not the contained boolean.

children.label: Comparisons
children.note: An empty optional equals nullopt and is less than every value.

children.label: variant basics
children.note: Exactly one of a fixed list of alternatives, with index() saying which.

children.label: Default construction
children.note: Holds a value-initialized first alternative; put monostate first if that type has no default constructor.

children.label: get versus get_if
children.note: get throws bad_variant_access on mismatch; get_if takes a pointer and returns null.

children.label: visit and overloaded
children.note: visit with an overloaded lambda set forces every alternative to be handled at compile time.

children.label: variant conversions
children.note: How a value picks an alternative, and what happens when that goes wrong.

children.label: Converting constructor
children.note: Overload resolution over the alternatives; ties make the constructor unavailable.

children.label: Narrowing excluded
children.note: Since the C++20 fix, narrowing candidates are dropped, so a literal no longer picks bool.

children.label: valueless_by_exception
children.note: A throw during a type change can leave no value; index() is then variant_npos.

children.label: any
children.note: A type-erased box holding a copy of any copy-constructible value.

children.label: Decayed storage
children.note: any a = "hi" holds a const char*, not a std::string.

children.label: Copy requirement
children.note: The decayed type must be copy constructible, so move-only types are rejected.

children.label: Small buffer
children.note: Implementations are encouraged but not required to avoid allocating for small types.

children.label: any_cast forms
children.note: Value and reference forms throw bad_any_cast; the pointer form returns null.

children.label: Choosing
children.note: Pick by how much the type system knows about the alternatives.

children.label: Closed set
children.note: Use variant when you can list the types; it is checked at compile time.

children.label: Open set
children.note: Use any only when the types are genuinely unknown, and expect a run-time check.
